Save traceable GBIF occurrences for local mapping

Source: R/spatial_gbif.R
gbif_save_occurrences.Rd

Supply exactly one of species or taxon_id. GBIF resolves a supplied name as an exact species-level name or validates a COL XR usage key as an exact species-level taxon, then retrieves georeferenced records using that taxon key and the same checklist key. By default, the fast occurrence-search API retrieves up to 50,000 records without waiting for a registered download. Set generate_doi = TRUE to wait for a registered download and include its official DOI in metadata.json; this requires GBIF_USER, GBIF_PWD, and GBIF_EMAIL credentials. With generate_doi = TRUE, set limit = NULL to save all available records; otherwise increase the finite limit up to 100,000. For high-volume species such as Amaranthus hybridus, prefer a local export or narrow the query with date or spatial filters. Country areas are queried with GBIF's standardized country predicate; crop_vector and crop_box are converted to a common WGS 84 geometry and sent as a spatial predicate. The exact package boundary is applied to returned records before limit, so a crop receives up to the requested number of matching occurrences. If a vector geometry exceeds GBIF's query-size limit, its bounding box is used as a candidate filter and the exact geometry is applied locally. The function can optionally restrict records to a KML or ESRI Shapefile boundary, a named geographic area, or a WGS 84 bounding box. It saves the returned GBIF fields and machine-readable metadata including the exact taxon match and COL XR taxon key, and, for a crop, the corresponding WGS 84 boundary. Full-extent exports can be used offline with source = "local" in gbif_map() or gbif_map_crop(). A cropped export can be used with gbif_map_crop() by selecting source = "local", local_export = "crop", and the same crop arguments used when saving it. When both functions use the same taxon, occurrence set, and crop selectors, their saved occurrence records are interchangeable as local input. The default limit is 50,000; limit = NULL requires generate_doi = TRUE to save the complete available occurrence set. The default fast search saves the returned records without waiting for a registered GBIF download. Set generate_doi = TRUE to wait for that download and record its DOI in the metadata. In either form, the accepted COL XR species name determines the output directory, so supplying a taxon by name or by taxon_id uses the same path.

gbif_save_occurrences(
  species = NULL,
  crop_vector = NULL,
  crop_area = NULL,
  crop_box = NULL,
  limit = 50000L,
  directory = getwd(),
  overwrite = TRUE,
  taxon_id = NULL,
  generate_doi = FALSE,
  date = NULL
)

gbif_save_ocurrences(
  species = NULL,
  crop_vector = NULL,
  crop_area = NULL,
  crop_box = NULL,
  limit = 50000L,
  directory = getwd(),
  overwrite = TRUE,
  taxon_id = NULL,
  generate_doi = FALSE,
  date = NULL
)

Arguments

species

A binomial scientific name, for example "Bidens andicola". GBIF must resolve it as an exact species-level name; approximate or higher-rank matches are not used. Supply exactly one of species or taxon_id.

crop_vector

Optional path to a .kml or .shp file used to restrict occurrences to a geographic area. The file name provides the place name used for the caption and export directory. It cannot be combined with crop_area.

crop_area, crop_box

Geographic crop selectors shared with gbif_map_crop(). They use the same area resolution, WGS 84 coordinate order, label, and overlap rules. Here they filter the records being saved and determine the Place subdirectory. A country area uses GBIF's standardized country predicate when its two-letter code is available; crop_box is sent as a WGS 84 spatial predicate. crop_area cannot be combined with crop_vector; crop_box can be used alone or with either boundary input.

limit

Maximum number of georeferenced records retained after the spatial filter, as a positive integer from 1 to 100000. Defaults to 50000, as in gbif_map_crop(). Set to NULL with generate_doi = TRUE to retrieve all available matching records. For high-volume species, use a local export or narrow the query with date or a spatial selector.

directory

Base output directory. As in gbif_map_crop(), the function creates sacha_exports/Family_Genus_species; cropped exports are placed in its Place subdirectory. Defaults to getwd().

overwrite

Logical. If TRUE (default), existing occurrence, metadata, and boundary files for this export may be replaced; FALSE prevents replacement.

taxon_id

A COL XR alphanumeric species usage key, such as "Q2M4". GBIF verifies that the key identifies one species-level taxon. Supply exactly one of taxon_id or species.

generate_doi

Logical. If TRUE, request and wait for a registered GBIF occurrence download, and record its DOI in metadata.json. This requires GBIF account credentials. If FALSE (default), retrieve records with the faster occurrence-search API and save the returned records without waiting for a DOI.

date

Optional ISO date or date range such as "2020-01-01,2021-01-01". It filters occurrence datasets by their GBIF registry creation date (createdDate), then selects records from those datasets. It does not filter the date an occurrence was observed.

Value

A named character vector with paths to the saved occurrence, metadata, and, for cropped exports, boundary files.

Details

Full-extent records are saved to sacha_exports/Family_Genus_species; cropped records are saved to sacha_exports/Family_Genus_species/Place, where Place is derived from the crop-vector file name, the resolved geographic area, or the crop-box label (or its coordinates when no label is supplied).

GBIF uses the Catalogue of Life Extended Release (COL XR) as the taxonomic reference for occurrence downloads. By downloading the data, you acknowledge GBIF's data-use agreement. When citing or referring to registered downloads (generate_doi = TRUE), follow GBIF's citation guidelines and include the DOI assigned to that specific download in every publication.

Configure the GBIF account credentials in the current R session with Sys.setenv(GBIF_USER = "your_username", GBIF_PWD = "your_password", GBIF_EMAIL = "your_account_email"). To keep them available in future sessions, add the same three variables to your personal ~/.Renviron file and restart R. Do not share or publish that file.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
gbif_save_occurrences("Bidens andicola")
gbif_save_occurrences("Bidens andicola", crop_vector = "Cotopaxi.kml")
gbif_save_occurrences(taxon_id = "Q2M4")
gbif_save_occurrences(
  "Bidens andicola",
  crop_box = c(-75, -10, -70, -5, "study area"),
  limit = 5000
)
gbif_map("Bidens andicola", source = "local")
} # }
